title: THE TWO-TRAY TEST
name: THE TWO-TRAY TEST
goal: A loud conclusion still has to pass inspection.
steps:
1. Imagine Trays — Imagine two trays.
2. Name Sides — Name the left SUPPORTS IT and the right DOESN’T FIT.
3. Sort Facts — Drop only visible facts into them—no feelings disguised as evidence.
4. Switch Sides — Now cover the fuller tray and read the neglected one silently.
5. Balance Verdict — Finish with a verdict that can hold both sides without pretending they weigh the same.
win: ✓ Both trays stayed visible; the verdict stopped being one-sided.
winReward: ✓ Both trays stayed visible; the verdict stopped being one-sided.
supports:
• Exhale after “Balance Verdict”; let feeling settle.
• Use “Sort Facts” on return.
• “Switch Sides” separates feeling from fact.
• “Imagine Trays” → “Balance Verdict”: what changed?
• I can use “Name Sides” while emotion stays loud.
formulaFlow: Imagine Trays → Name Sides → Sort Facts → Switch Sides → Balance Verdict
safety:
PAUSE
Quit when you are recycling arguments instead of discovering evidence.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WORST CASE, WITH EXITS
name: WORST CASE, WITH EXITS
goal: A worst-case story loses size when it gains a route.
steps:
1. Name Fear — Picture the feared ending in one line.
2. Build Exits — Under it build four rungs: WHAT HAPPENS; WHAT I DO NEXT; WHO OR WHAT HELPS; HOW RECOVERY COULD BEGIN.
3. Add Likely — Add a fifth rung for the outcome that is actually most likely.
4. Climb Route — Move through the five steps once in your mind.
5. Act Now — Then take the first coping action available now.
win: ✓ The forecast lost its monopoly.
winReward: ✓ The forecast lost its monopoly.
supports:
• Exhale after “Act Now”; leave the forecast.
• Shortcut: “Add Likely”, once.
• “Climb Route” — fear isn’t fate.
• What lost power: “Name Fear” → “Act Now”?
• I can use “Build Exits” while fear stays loud.
formulaFlow: Name Fear → Build Exits → Add Likely → Climb Route → Act Now
safety:
PAUSE
Do not run this alone for immediate danger, medical crisis, or trauma flooding.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE ODDS RECEIPT
name: THE ODDS RECEIPT
goal: Fear speaks in certainty; reality keeps percentages.
steps:
1. Score Odds — Give the prediction a number from 0 to 100.
2. Check Baseline — Find one real reference point: how often has this happened in similar situations?
3. Weigh Evidence — Notice one fact that raises the odds and another that lowers them.
4. Revise Odds — Pick a new number and remember it.
5. Follow Evidence — Act from the revision, not the original alarm.
win: ✓ Disaster stopped being the only ending.
winReward: ✓ Disaster stopped being the only ending.
supports:
• Exhale after “Follow Evidence”; leave the forecast.
• Loop back? Use “Weigh Evidence”.
• “Revise Odds” — fear isn’t fate.
• What lost power: “Score Odds” → “Follow Evidence”?
• I can use “Check Baseline” while fear stays loud.
formulaFlow: Score Odds → Check Baseline → Weigh Evidence → Revise Odds → Follow Evidence
safety:
PAUSE
End the count if numbers become reassurance checking or you cannot stop recalculating.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE BLAME PIE
name: THE BLAME PIE
goal: Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.
steps:
1. Imagine A Pie — Imagine a pie that stands for everything that caused the situation.
2. Share The Slices — In your mind, give slices to your choices, other people, circumstances, systems, timing, and chance.
3. Check The Whole — Make sure all slices together equal 100.
4. Find Your Slice — Focus only on your true share.
5. Choose Repair — Picture one repair for your slice. Let the rest stay outside your responsibility.
win: ✓ My slice stayed mine; the rest went back to the whole pie.
winReward: ✓ My slice stayed mine; the rest went back to the whole pie.
supports:
• Exhale after “Choose Repair”; release extra blame.
• Pulled back? Touch “Check The Whole”.
• “Find Your Slice” keeps blame in proportion.
• Compare “Imagine A Pie” with “Choose Repair”.
• I can use “Share The Slices” without owning everything.
formulaFlow: Imagine A Pie → Share The Slices → Check The Whole → Find Your Slice → Choose Repair
safety:
PAUSE
Set it down if sharing turns into punishment or erases genuine accountability.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WORD MELT
name: WORD MELT
goal: Repeat the sound until the spell loses its language.
steps:
1. Choose Charged — Choose one charged word—not a whole painful story.
2. Say Gently — Say it gently and steadily for about twenty seconds.
3. Listen Moment — Listen for the moment it becomes rhythm, mouth movement, or noise.
4. Stop Room — Stop there and look around the room.
5. Return Seen — Meaning may return; you have seen it separate once.
win: ✓ The word lost its spell; I heard sound without obeying meaning.

title: PLAY THE BODY PASSWORD
name: PLAY THE BODY PASSWORD
goal: A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.
steps:

PLAY TIME
45–60 seconds

GOAL
A large release can become several manageable ones.

RITUAL
1. Let Air — Instead of one continuous out-breath, let air leave in three soft portions with tiny unforced spaces between.
2. Keep Face — Keep the face loose and never push to empty.
3. Wait Body — After the final segment, wait for the body’s next inhale rather than grabbing it.

WIN
✓ The narrative stopped owning every room.

SUPPORTS
• Exhale after “Wait Body”; then keep moving.
• If it flares, choose “Keep Face”.
• “Keep Face” proves motion is available.
• Difference check: “Let Air” → “Wait Body”.
• I can use “Keep Face” before motivation.

FORMULA FLOW
Let Air → Keep Face → Wait Body

SAFETY
PAUSE
Resume normal breathing if segmentation causes urgency or tingling.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE RETURN REP
name: THE RETURN REP
goal: Attention strengthens on the comeback, not the stay.

title: BREAK THE NIGHT'S STORYLINE
name: BREAK THE NIGHT'S STORYLINE
goal: Sleep does not need another storyline to solve.
steps:

4. Jump Letter — Jump to the next letter and a completely unrelated object. End after five letters; do not score sleep.

PLAY TIME
45–60 seconds

GOAL
Language can lower heat without lowering truth.

RITUAL
1. Underline — Underline absolutes and inflammatory terms in your account.
2. Observe Behaviour — Exchange every one for a precise factual equivalent: ‘always’ becomes the actual frequency; ‘destroyed’ becomes the specific loss; ‘evil’ becomes the observed behaviour.
3. Read Action — Re-read and notice what action the cooler version supports.

WIN
✓ The facts stayed; the heat came down.

SUPPORTS
• Exhale after “Read Action”; then keep moving.
• If it flares, choose “Observe Behaviour”.
• “Observe Behaviour” proves motion is available.
• “Underline” versus “Read Action”: what eased?
• I can use “Observe Behaviour” before motivation.

FORMULA FLOW
Underline → Observe Behaviour → Read Action

SAFETY
PAUSE
Retain strong moral language when accurate naming is necessary.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CAPTURE THE MODEL’S MISS
name: CAPTURE THE MODEL’S MISS
goal: Reality’s surprise is premium evidence.
steps:
1. Keep Both Versions — The moment an outcome differs from expectation, keep both versions verbatim.
2. State Size — State the size and direction of the error.
3. Name Miss — Finish with: ‘The old model must now explain…’ and name the discrepancy.
4. Preserve Forecast — Do not let hindsight rewrite the original prediction.
win: ✓ Original prediction preserved. Hindsight cannot edit the miss now.
winReward: ✓ Original prediction preserved. Hindsight cannot edit the miss now.

title: MAKE FEAR NAME A DEADLINE
name: MAKE FEAR NAME A DEADLINE
goal: A warning must become testable before it can command you.
steps:
1. Pin Forecast — Restate the fear as one visible or audible prediction—not a vague catastrophe.
2. Set Clock — Give the prediction a real time window.
3. Score Odds — Set confidence on a 0–100 scale before checking anything.
4. Observe Safely — Use only a naturally occurring safe observation; never manufacture a test.
5. Update Odds — Hold the result and update confidence in either direction.
win: ✓ The next move no longer has to obey the loudest second.
winReward: ✓ The next move no longer has to obey the loudest second.
supports:
• Exhale after “Update Odds”; leave the forecast.
• On return: “Score Odds”.
• “Observe Safely” — fear isn’t fate.
• What lost power: “Pin Forecast” → “Update Odds”?
• I can use “Set Clock” while fear stays loud.

safety:
PAUSE

title: FIND THE MOVE NO FEELING MUST BETRAY
name: FIND THE MOVE NO FEELING MUST BETRAY
goal: Inner agreement is optional; a move that betrays no red line is enough.
steps:
1. Seat Feelings — Label up to three active emotions as players at the table. Leave them unnamed for the moment; observe first.
2. Vetoes — Give each emotion one veto: ‘Fear will not accept ___. Anger will not accept ___. Sadness will not accept ___.’
3. Clear Board — Cross out actions blocked by any safe, reasonable veto. Ignore demands for harm, punishment, or impossible certainty. Put it into simple words a child could understand.
4. Choose Survivor — Choose one remaining action that crosses no red line, even if no feeling loves it.
win: ✓ No feeling agreed, but no red line had to be betrayed.
winReward: ✓ No feeling agreed, but no red line had to be betrayed.

• I can use “Vetoes” without extra heat.

title: GIVE THE BELIEF A POSTCODE
name: GIVE THE BELIEF A POSTCODE
goal: A rule may fit one situation without ruling your whole life.
steps:
1. Name The Belief — Say the belief silently.
2. Imagine Four Limits — Think about when, where, with whom, and under what conditions it may be true.
3. Test Inside — Picture one real case where it fits.
4. Test Outside — Picture one real case where it does not fit.
5. Shrink the Rule — Say a smaller, more accurate version of the belief.
win: ✓ The belief got a postcode instead of a passport to everywhere.
